Beijing sets the oil price now more than OPEC does.

During the worst energy crisis in years, China cut crude imports 40%, from 11.6 million barrels a day in 2025 to about 7 million by June. A single-country drop that size has never happened, and China's economy still grew 4.3%.

China has become the OPEC of demand. It drained its own stockpile instead of paying up, and it can keep imports this low for six more months on 1.1 billion barrels in storage. That elasticity is what capped crude and pulled the 10-year yield back from its highs.

The next oil spike will not come from a supply headline. It comes the day Beijing's stockpile nears its refill line around 1.07 billion barrels and China walks back in to buy. That is when oil reprices higher and the pressure lands back on yields and long-duration stocks.

$USO

The bull case for Big Tech rests on one spreadsheet assumption.

Wall Street's models put the five hyperscalers' operating margin at 31% in 2029, up from 27% in 2025, even as they spend trillions on AI. Half of that gain requires overhead, SG&A, to fall from 10% to 8% of revenue while revenue nearly doubles past $3 trillion.

That is a $77 billion assumed efficiency, and it has never happened at this growth rate. Depreciation from the new data centers is about to soar, and Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet are already free-cash-flow negative.

The multiples are priced on a forecast that overhead shrinks while revenue doubles. If AI does not deliver that cost cut, margins compress and the whole valuation breaks.

It's been almost 2 months since I have cut down my screen time by 90%.

I no longer scroll social media, watch youtube, netflix, etc. No more video games.

I'm close to the happiest I've ever been. The only thing missing is the "work" or "productivity" element to my life atm. I am procrastinating a lot of things that have been on my to-do list for a long time.

A lot of emails and messages I need to respond to. A lot of admin work. A lot of community work. Some mistakes I made with yoshizen I need to figure out how to make up for. Tax stuff.

It's all piling up and I know I need to get to it soon but I cannot for the life of me find the motivation. I can't shake the dread I feel at the thought of sitting down at my computer for hours and hours.

It's funny. Being addicted to screens and dopamine is not a good thing, but removing them from my life, while overall a net positive, has also removed my ability to spend any time with the devices that rule our lives.

God damn it's hard to find balance.

Dunno if anyone out there has been through anything similar and come out the other side, but I am all ears for any tips or suggestions for re-finding purpose or motivation

This is true. It’s still striking to me how many people expect AI compute prices to fall simply because new capacity keeps coming online.

The demand side is digital. The supply side is physical.

Demand can grow almost exponentially overnight especially as models improve. Supply is constrained by GPUs, HBM, power, transformers, electricians, data centers, permitting… (and a hundred other bottlenecks).

In this market, GPU prices are ultimately driven by the value they unlock, not just by the cost of the hardware.

So for example: 

Company A uses GPUs to summarize internal emails. Great, it saves thousands of hours so millions of dollars. 

Company B uses those same GPUs to discover a new drug or make a scientific breakthrough worth tens of billions. Company B will simply outbid Company A. 

As AI expands into more frontier use cases with enormous economic value, the willingness to pay for the newest compute keeps increasing. So even as supply grows, don’t be surprised if frontier compute remains expensive, or even gets more expensive!
